- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After recent price spikes, model often overshoots downward in the next few days; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged sell pressure.  
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized in model; if price is 20%+ above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overcorrection.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in first 5–7 days of 30d horizon; apply smoothing or lagged adjustment to reduce initial overreaction.
